text:
A 24-year-old woman who was born and raised in London believing she was a UK citizen has been left in a state of shock after being told by authorities that she is not British.
After the Home Office discovered that the woman’s mother, who is from Jamaica, had no right to a British passport, she received a letter informing her her UK passport was being revoked.
She no longer has the right to work or rent a property and says she is facing homelessness and destitution.
The rules around who is eligible for British citizenship are complex and being born in the UK does not automatically entitle a person to it. Instead it is determined by when a person was born and their parents’ circumstances.
“As your mother and father were not British citizens at the time of your birth you have no claim to British nationality or entitlement to the passports issued,” the Home Office said in their letter.
The woman, who does not wish to be publicly named, was born at Guy’s and St Thomas’ hospital in London and was brought up in the capital. She struggled with her education due an unstable family life. Her mother spent periods in prison for drug-related offences and as a result she spent time in care, including a short period with family in Jamaica, and on the child protection register.
But she was determined to make something of her life worked hard at school, and secured a good job. “I have always believed I’m British. The UK is my home and the only home I have,” she told the Guardian.
“I don’t want to leave the UK and move to Jamaica, a place I hardly know. I want to continue with my life in the UK. I’ve lost everything because the Home Office is punishing me for my mum’s actions. I’m trying to find a way forward but this has been a horrendous change in my life.”
A legal challenge against the passport revocation has been rejected by the Home Office. Officials said they had acted lawfully. “Where evidence comes to light that citizenship or a British passport has been obtained on the basis of fraud or false information, we will take appropriate action in accordance with the law,” a Home Office spokesperson said.
When asked if officials were planning to deport the woman to Jamaica, Home Office sources said that any action concerning an individual’s immigration status or removal from the UK would be considered on the particular circumstances of their case.
The woman’s solicitor, Naga Kandiah of MTC Solicitors, said: “She was born and raised in the UK, educated here, and has held a British passport since birth. Britain is the only home she has ever known. To suddenly have her identity and citizenship called into question is devastating. She is innocent of any wrongdoing, yet she is the one being made to suffer. This decision raises profound questions of fairness and justice and could have serious implications for others in similar circumstances.”
A spokesperson for the Project for the Registration of Children as British Citizens said: “The government must urgently do two things. First, it must take steps to ensure people can get on with their lives as swiftly as possible by resolving their citizenship. Second, it must raise awareness of citizenship rights so that far fewer people find themselves in this dreadful situation.”
digest_he:
צעירה בת 24 שנולדה וגדלה בלונדון קיבלה מכתב מפתיע ממשרד הפנים הבריטי לפיו דרכונה הבריטי יבוטל וכי אינה נחשבת לאזרחית המדינה. הרשויות גילו כי אמה, ילידת ג'מייקה, לא הייתה זכאית לדרכון בריטי בעת לידתה, עובדה שהשאירה את הצעירה ללא זכות חוקית לעבוד או לשכור דירה. הצעירה, שעבדה קשה כדי להצליח למרות ילדותה הלא יציבה, הביעה זעזוע עמוק וציינה כי בריטניה היא הבית היחיד שהיא מכירה.

עורכי דינה של הצעירה טענו כי מדובר בהחלטה קורעת לב שפוגעת באדם חף מפשע שמעולם לא הכיר מציאות אחרת. משרד הפנים מסר בתגובה כי הפעולות נעשו כחוק כאשר מתגלה מרמה או מידע שגוי בהנפקת דרכונים, וכי כל שאלה בנוגע לגירוש תיבחן לפי הנסיבות. ארגונים חברתיים קראו לממשלה לפתור מיד את מצבם של האנשים הנקלעים לסבך הבירוקרטי הזה ולספק להם ודאות.
